extracted.intended_audience: USCIS petitioners/registrants, immigration attorneys, employers and representatives filing H-1B (and related H-class) petitions
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards governing H-1B (and related H-class) registration, weighted/random selection, filing, evidentiary and validity requirements, cap exemptions, and numerical allocation procedures for petitioners and registrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique beneficiary counting
rubrics_metrics.description: Each unique beneficiary will only be counted once toward the numerical allocation projections, regardless of how many registrations were submitted for that beneficiary or how many times the beneficiary is entered in the selection pool.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will separately notify each registrant whose registration on behalf of a beneficiary has been selected. A petitioner may file an H-1B cap-subject petition only after that beneficiary's properly submitted registration has been selected for that fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required information on registration (wage level and identifiers)
rubrics_metrics.description: On the registration, the registrant must select the highest OEWS wage level that the beneficiary's proffered wage equals or exceeds for the relevant SOC code and provide identifying/position information and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proffered wage is lower than OEWS wage level I because it's based on another legitimate source, select 'wage level I.' For multiple locations or multiple positions (agent), select the lowest corresponding OEWS wage level the proffered wage will equal/exceed. If wage is a range, select the OEWS level that the lowest wage equals/exceeds. If no OEWS data exists, select the level using Department of Labor prevailing wage guidance. Registrant must also provide SOC code, area(s) of intended employment used for wage basis, beneficiary passport/travel document information, and all other requested information and certifications. Each beneficiary must be registered under only one valid passport/travel document and, if abroad, the passport info must correspond to the passport intended for U.S. entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weighted selection by OEWS wage level
rubrics_metrics.description: If a random selection is necessary, each unique beneficiary is assigned to the lowest OEWS wage level among all registrations submitted on the beneficiary's behalf and entered into the selection pool in a weighted manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weighting: wage level IV = entered 4 times; level III = 3 times; level II = 2 times; level I = 1 time. This assignment uses the lowest wage level across registrations for that beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting registrations for regular cap
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will consider all properly submitted registrations relating to beneficiaries that may be counted under section 214(g)(1)(A) of the Act, including those that may also be eligible for exemption under section 214(g)(5)(C) of the Act; registrations will be counted based on the number of unique beneficiaries registered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This governs whether there are enough registrations to meet the H-1B regular cap and interacts with the weighted selection rules when random selection is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when fewer registrations than needed (regular cap)
rubrics_metrics.description: If at the end of the initial registration period there are fewer unique beneficiaries with properly submitted registrations than needed to meet the H-1B regular cap, USCIS will notify all petitioners with properly registered beneficiaries that their registrations have been selected and will keep the registration period open until sufficient registrations are received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will monitor unique beneficiary count and notify the public of the 'final registration date' when sufficient registrations have been received. The day of public notice does not control the final registration date. If more registrations exist on the final registration date than needed, USCIS will apply weighting and randomly select the number of unique beneficiaries necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when sufficient registrations (regular cap)
rubrics_metrics.description: If at the end of the initial registration period USCIS determines there are more than sufficient unique beneficiaries to meet the regular cap, USCIS will stop accepting registrations and notify the public of the final registration date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will weight each unique beneficiary per the wage-level weighting scheme and randomly select the number of unique beneficiaries necessary to meet the H-1B regular cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced degree exemption selection rules
rubrics_metrics.description: After determining it will no longer accept registrations under the regular cap, USCIS will determine whether remaining registrations suffice to meet the H-1B advanced degree exemption numerical limitation and apply selection rules accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fewer unique beneficiaries exist than needed, USCIS will notify petitioners and keep accepting registrations until sufficient numbers are reached; if more than sufficient, USCIS will stop accepting registrations and weight and randomly select as necessary. The final registration date and weighting/random selection rules operate similarly to the regular cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reserve list and reopening registration to increase allocations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unselected properly submitted registrations for unique beneficiaries remain on reserve for the fiscal year; USCIS may select from reserves or reopen registration to increase numbers projected to meet allocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If USCIS needs more registrations to meet regular cap or advanced degree exemption allocations, it will select sufficient unique beneficiaries from the reserve according to prior selection rules. If all on reserve are selected and still insufficient, USCIS may reopen the registration period and will announce the reopened period start on uscis.gov. USCIS will notify the public of any new 'final registration date' and the public notice date does not control the final date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmation of registration acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitioners will receive electronic notification that USCIS has accepted a registration for processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to file H-1B cap-subject petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will notify petitioners with selected registrations that the petitioner is eligible to file an H-1B cap-subject petition on behalf of the beneficiary within the filing period shown on the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing procedures tied to a valid registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner may file an H-1B petition only if the petition is based on a valid registration properly submitted according to §103.2, the registration tool instructions, and the relevant regulatory paragraph, and submitted by the petitioner or its designated representative on behalf of the selected beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petitioner may not substitute the beneficiary named in the original registration or transfer the registration to another petitioner. The H-1B petition must contain and be supported by the same identifying and position information (including SOC code) provided in the selected registration and the LCA, and must include a proffered wage that equals or exceeds the prevailing wage for the OEWS wage level indicated on the registration. Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis for the wage level as of the registration date and evidence of the passport/travel document used at registration. USCIS may, in its discretion, permit certain changes (e.g., legal name change due to marriage, passport renewal) or area(s) of intended employment changes if consistent with a bona fide job offer, but may deny or revoke petitions that do not meet these requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration fee requirement and effect of invalid fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The registration fee is non-refundable and due at submission; USCIS may deny or revoke the approval of an H-1B petition if the registration fee is declined, not reconciled, disputed, or otherwise invalid after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing period for cap-subject petition
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B cap-subject petition must be properly filed within the filing period indicated on the selection notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The filing period will be at least 90 days. Failure to meet paragraph (h)(8)(iii)(D) requirements may lead USCIS to deny or reject the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating number of registrations needed to meet caps
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating the number of registrations for unique beneficiaries needed to meet the regular cap and the advanced degree exemption numerical limitation for a fiscal year, USCIS will take into account historical data and other relevant factors and may increase those numbers during the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors include historical approvals, denials, revocations, and other relevant elements that inform projections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and criteria for cap exemptions (214(g)(5)(A)/(B))
rubrics_metrics.description: For cap-exemption determinations, 'Institution of higher education' uses the Higher Education Act definition; a nonprofit entity is considered related/affiliated with an institution of higher education if it meets specified connection/operation/attachment/formal affiliation conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nonprofit entity affiliation qualifies under any one of: shared ownership/control by same board or federation; operated by an institution; attached as member/branch/cooperative/subsidiary; or a formal written affiliation agreement establishing an active working relationship for research or education with fundamental activities directly contributing to the institution's research/education mission. 'Nonprofit entity', 'nonprofit research organization', and 'governmental research organization' have specified cross-referenced definitions in the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial work-time and duties test for cap-exemption
rubrics_metrics.description: An H-1B beneficiary who is not directly employed by a qualifying institution may qualify for cap exemption if they will spend at least half of their work time performing job duties at a qualifying entity and those duties directly further a fundamental mission (higher education, nonprofit research, governmental research).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work performed 'at' the qualifying institution may include telework/remote/off-site work. USCIS focuses on the job duties to be performed rather than physical location when determining cap-exempt status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of cessation or conversion of cap-exempt employment
rubrics_metrics.description: If cap-exempt employment ceases and the alien is not the beneficiary of a new cap-exempt petition, the alien will be subject to the cap unless previously counted within the relevant 6-year period; conversion from cap-exempt to cap-subject employment may lead USCIS to revoke the petition authorizing such employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS may revoke petitions consistent with paragraph (h)(11)(iii) when conversion or cessation issues arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent H-1B employment and cap treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Concurrent H-1B employment in a cap-subject position of an alien that qualifies for an exemption shall not subject the alien to the numerical limitations if conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must demonstrate: the beneficiary is employed in valid H-1B status under a cap exemption; the cap-exempt employment is expected to continue after the new cap-subject petition is approved; and the beneficiary can reasonably and concurrently perform the work described in each employer's positions. The validity of the concurrent cap-subject petition cannot extend beyond the cap-exempt H-1B employment period. If cap-exempt employment terminates early, the alien becomes subject to the cap unless previously counted or another exemption applies; USCIS may revoke the cap-subject petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension of registration process
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may suspend the H-1B registration requirement if it determines the registration process is inoperable for any reason.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If suspended, USCIS will announce the suspension and the opening date of the applicable H-1B cap-subject petition-filing period on uscis.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition-based cap-subject selection when registration suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: In years where registration is suspended, USCIS will accept H-1B petitions and conduct selection based on petitions received, applying similar wage-level selection and weighting rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must select the highest OEWS wage level the proffered wage equals/exceeds (with same rules for lower-than-level-I, multiple locations, wage ranges, and DOL guidance when no OEWS data). If random selection is necessary, weight petitions by OEWS level (IV=4, III=3, II=2, I=1) and select via computer-generated selection. Petitioners must submit evidence of the basis for the selected wage level as of the petition date. USCIS will deny petitions claiming cap-exemption if determined ineligible after final receipt date; if determined ineligible on or before the final receipt date, USCIS may consider the petition under the applicable numerical allocation. Denied petitions under this paragraph do not receive returned/refunded filing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular cap selection rules when registration suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: When registration is suspended, USCIS will consider all properly submitted petitions relating to beneficiaries countable under section 214(g)(1)(A) and will compute projections and a 'final receipt date' for meeting the regular cap.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS uses historical data and other factors for projections, monitors petitions received, and announces the date it receives the number projected as needed (the 'final receipt date'). The announcement date does not control the final receipt date. If the final receipt date falls on any of the first five business days that filings could be received and the numerical limit is reached on one of those days, USCIS will weight petitions and randomly select the number necessary from petitions filed during the first five business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advanced degree exemption selection when registration suspended
rubrics_metrics.description: After completing the regular-cap petition selection in a suspended-registration year, USCIS will determine whether remaining petitions suffice for the advanced degree exemption and apply similar projection/selection rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS will account for historical data and other relevant factors, monitor petitions, announce a final receipt date, and apply weighting/random selection if the final receipt date occurs within the first five business days as described.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability of registration and selection provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement to submit a registration and the selection process based on properly submitted registrations are intended to be severable from petition-based selection provisions; other specific provisions (beneficiary-centric selection, requested start date removal, denial/revocation for fraud/misrepresentation) are intended to be severable from one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, DHS intends that other provisions continue in effect to the maximum extent permitted by law; wholly invalid provisions should be severed without affecting other applicable provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-1C numerical limitations allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: 500 H-1C nonimmigrant visas issued each fiscal year are allocated among states with per-state ceilings and special quarter/usage rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Caps: certain large states (CA, FL, IL, MI, NY, OH, PA, TX) limited to 50 each; other states limited to 25 each. If total visas available during first three quarters exceed approvable petitions then visas may be issued in last quarter to nurses in states whose cap has been reached. Facilities must notify the Service if an approved H-1C petition is not used; revoked approvals may be subtracted from total count if alien never commenced employment; if an H-1C petition lists more nurses than available for remainder of fiscal year, Service approves allowable amount in order listed and remaining beneficiaries considered in next fiscal year. Once 500 cap reached, Service will reject new petitions requesting work start date prior to next fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-2B numerical limitation and selection procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: When calculating numerical limits under section 214(g)(1)(B) and 214(g)(10), USCIS will make numbers available in order of filing, project needed petitions using historical data, monitor petitions received, and may randomly select among petitions received on the final receipt date if necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USCIS announces the final receipt date (announcement date does not control final receipt date). Petitions not randomly selected or received after the final receipt date will be rejected. Petitions claiming exemption that are determined after final receipt date to be subject to the limit will be denied and fees not refunded. If final receipt date falls on any of the first five business days filings can be made and numerical limit is reached on any of those days, USCIS will randomly apply numbers among petitions received on any of those five business days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval standards and Notice of Action contents
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will consider all evidence submitted and any other evidence independently required to assist adjudication; approval is notified on a Notice of Action that includes beneficiary name(s), classification, and petition validity period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition for more than one beneficiary or multiple services may be approved in whole or in part. If approved for less time than requested, the approval notice will provide or be accompanied by a brief explanation of the validity period granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recording validity period rules for approved petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures determine how approval dates/validity periods are recorded depending on approval timing relative to requested start date and stated limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If approved before requested begin date, show actual dates requested (not to exceed limits). If approved after requested begin date, validity commences with approval date and ends with requested date (within limits). If requested period exceeds allowed limit, approve only up to that limit. USCIS may issue an RFE to ask petitioner if they want to update requested dates when petition is approvable after originally requested end date; factors informing RFE include additional petitions or beneficiary eligibility for additional time. If new requested period exceeds LCA validity, petitioner must submit a certified LCA with new validity corresponding to the requested period and an updated prevailing/proffered wage if applicable (petitioner may not reduce proffered wage). The LCA may be certified after petition filing. Requests for new dates and submission of corresponding LCA, absent other changes, are not considered a material change. An increase to the proffered wage is not a material change if no other material changes exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: RFE non-response and effect on downstream benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: If USCIS does not issue an RFE concerning requested dates of employment, or if petitioner does not respond or the response does not support new dates, the petition will be approved (if otherwise approvable) for the originally requested period or until the end-date eligibility is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the petition will not be forwarded to the Department of State nor will any accompanying request for change of status, extension of stay, or amendment of stay be granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity periods by petition type
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial approval periods for H petitions conform to prescribed limits depending on classification and circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: H-1B specialty occupation up to 3 years but not exceeding LCA validity; H-1B for DOD R&D or coproduction up to 5 years; H-1B for distinguished fashion models up to 3 years; H-2B per approved temporary labor certification; H-3 alien trainee up to 2 years; H-3 special education program up to 18 months; H-1C registered nurse up to 3 years; petitions filed by U.S. employers where beneficiary owns controlling interest limited to up to 18 months initial approval and first extension also up to 18 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: H-4 dependent admission and employment authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Spouse and children of an H nonimmigrant accompanying or following to join may be admitted as H-4 nonimmigrants for the same period of admission or extension as the principal; H-4 status does not itself confer employment authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An H-4 nonimmigrant spouse of an H-1B nonimmigrant may be eligible for employment authorization only if the H-1B nonimmigrant is the beneficiary of an approved Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker (or successor form) or the H-1B nonimmigrant's period of stay in H-1B status is authorized in the U.S. under specified AC21 provisions. To request employment authorization, an eligible H-4 spouse must file an Application for Employment Authorization (or successor form) in accordance with 8 CFR 274a.13 and form instructions.
